newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU plays down subsidy link to Boeing merger plan.
newsitem.headline: EU plays down subsidy link to Boeing merger plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it discussed aviation subsidy rules with the United States, but denied the talks had anything to do with its anti-trust probe into Boeing Co's merger plans.

One Commission official told reporters on Monday that European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan had written to U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky about EU worries about subsidies to the U.S. civil aviation industry.

"All we are doing is asking for a review of the bilateral agreement...because we think that too many indirect subsidies are continuing to go into the American aviation industry. That's all we have done and that was six weeks ago," the official said. "That's not a renegotiation of the agreement, it's not a reopening of the agreement."

Aircraft subsidies are covered by a 1992 transatlantic agreement, which came in the face of accusations, both by Europe's Airbus Industrie and Boeing, that governments unfairly propped up their aircraft makers.
The subsidy questions come as European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert considers his options in reviewing the effects on the EU aircraft market of Boeing's merger with McDonnell Douglas.
Van Miert has said he dislikes the deal, in particular because of Boeing's exclusive-provider agreements with Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines.
A second Commission official denied on Monday that there was any link between talks on subsidies and the merger review process, telling reporters: "Those two issues are kept totally separate."

A U.S. source said Washington was not interested in reopening the subsidies debate and added that if that happened, Airbus might be worse off. The source added that, while there was no formal link between the subsidies and merger questions, there was a natural one that would have to be examined in the context of aid or perceived aid for space programmes and research and development work.
"Those might be areas where we could look for remedies to be applied, that's a natural link," the source added.
